newsitem.title: CHINA: First HK court case under China involves opium.
newsitem.headline: First HK court case under China involves opium.

text.p: In an eerie historical coincidence, the first court case in post-colonial Hong Kong involved opium -- heroin, anyway -- The South China Morning Post reported on Thursday.
It said Pang Moon-sing was accused of trafficking in 90 grams of heroin in Kowloon, now again part of China after a separation of more than 150 years caused by opium.
Britain, which had infuriated China by peddling opium to the Chinese, seized Hong Kong after winning the Opium War.
It finally returned Hong Kong to China at midnight on June 30, at the start of a week of celebrations marked by three days of holidays.
Pang was remanded in custody, the newspaper said.
